User Impersonation via Public Endpoint [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-287] on IAM Identity Center, Public Authentication Endpoint, IAM Roles: The public endpoint for user authentication may not properly validate user identity tokens or implement sufficient authentication controls, allowing attackers to forge or replay authentication requests. An attacker intercepts authentication requests, analyzes the token structure, and creates forged tokens to impersonate legitimate users.

Privilege Elevation via Token Spoofing [Tampering, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-269] on IAM Identity Center, IAM Roles, AWS Organizations: If token validation and identity propagation mechanisms are weak, attackers could modify token claims or attributes to gain access to higher-privileged roles. An attacker modifies the group membership claims in their identity token to gain admin privileges in connected AWS accounts.

Unauthorized Access to AWS Organizations [Information Disclosure, Access Control, CWE-284] on AWS Organizations, Network Infrastructure, IAM: Without proper VPC controls and network segmentation, internal AWS Organizations endpoints might be accessible from the public internet. An attacker discovers and attempts to access AWS Organizations management APIs directly from the internet, bypassing intended access controls.

Identity Synchronization Failure [Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, CWE-287] on IAM Identity Center, AWS Organizations, Corporate Identity Provider: Identity synchronization issues could result in stale or incorrect access permissions when users' roles or group memberships change. A terminated employee retains access to AWS resources due to failed identity synchronization between corporate directory and IAM Identity Center.

DDoS Attack on Authentication Endpoint [Denial of Service, CWE-400] on Public Authentication Endpoint, IAM Identity Center: Attackers could generate a large volume of authentication requests to overwhelm the service and prevent legitimate authentication attempts. A distributed botnet sends thousands of authentication requests per second to the endpoint, causing service degradation.

Insufficient Audit Logging [Repudiation, CWE-223] on CloudTrail, IAM Identity Center, DynamoDB Audit Logs: Incomplete logging configuration could create blind spots in audit trails, particularly for IAM Identity Center events. An attacker performs unauthorized actions through IAM Identity Center, but the activities are not logged for later investigation.

Insufficient Permission Boundaries [Elevation of Privilege, CWE-269] on AWS Organizations, IAM Roles, Member Accounts: Without proper permission boundaries through RCPs and SCPs, users or roles could gain more access than intended through IAM policy modifications. A compromised admin account in a member account creates overly permissive IAM roles due to missing SCP restrictions.
